title: ECD-Score: a Study on Erdheim-Chester Disease
off: Predicting Long-term Prognosis in Erdheim-Chester Disease: A New Comprehensive Approach
summary:
Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) is a rare form of non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis that primarily affects adults but may also occur in pediatric patients. It is characterized by the accumulation of foamy histiocytes with a distinctive immunophenotype in multiple anatomical sites, most commonly the long bones, retroperitoneal and perirenal tissues, the heart, the central nervous system, and the pituitary gland. The disease shows marked clinical heterogeneity, ranging from localized and asymptomatic forms to severe manifestations with multiorgan involvement. From a pathogenetic perspective, ECD is mainly driven by gain-of-function mutations affecting the MAPK and PI3K-AKT pathways, particularly the BRAFV600E mutation, leading to aberrant activation of the MAPK and mTOR signaling pathways. The release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines plays a key role in systemic inflammation and tissue damage, resulting in significant complications and disability depending on the organs involved.

Despite the significant efforts of international research in recent years, particularly given the extreme rarity of the disease (incidence below 5 cases per 10,000,000 adults per year), substantial knowledge gaps remain, especially with regard to the prediction of long-term outcomes, both in terms of survival and disability. Although some prognostic factors associated with survival have already been identified (such as central nervous system involvement), to date only limited-scale studies have systematically evaluated the prognosis of patients with ECD, focusing in particular on factors influencing organ-specific complications. Moreover, in clinical practice, several aspects that significantly affect patients' quality of life tend to be underestimated, partly due to the time required to perform comprehensive assessments using detailed questionnaires designed to quantify disease-related consequences, such as chronic disability, depression, and cognitive impairment. Nevertheless, there is a growing need for and interest in these parameters, commonly referred to as patient-reported outcomes. In light of these considerations, the development and implementation of a comprehensive prognostic score aimed at predicting survival and long-term disease outcomes could improve the overall assessment of patients and provide more accurate and clinically meaningful prognostic information.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* informed consent signed by the patient or, for minors, by a parent or legal guardian
* confirmed diagnosis of ECD according to the latest international guidelines (Goyal G, Blood 2020)
* availability of clinical, molecular, treatment and response to therapy data
* a minimum follow-up period of one year.

Exclusion Criteria:

* lack of diagnostic or follow-up data
* refusal or inability to sign the informed consent form

arms.d: Patients with ECD will be recruited and will attend outpatient visits at the study coordination center at the Meyer IRCCS University Hospital (Florence) and other participating centers. The patients to be enrolled will be "prevalent" and "incident" patients during the 5-year study period. Patients undergoing follow-up at their respective centers will be involved in the study, as well as those who receive a new diagnosis of ECD during the study period. Clinical data will be collected from all patients included, focusing primarily on organ involvement and response to treatment. They will also be asked to complete questionnaires on quality of life and other specific outcomes. Epidemiological data will also be considered, in particular the geographical origin of patients, and survival rates will also be evaluated.

primary.m: Association between belonging to a clinical cluster and survival
Association between organ damage and survival
Association between the treatment used (relative to the historical period) and survival
Association between response to treatment and survival
Association between treatment toxicity and survival
Association between geographical origin and survival

x.titre: Score pronostique dans la maladie d'Erdheim-Chester
x.question: Peut-on construire un score pronostique de la survie et des séquelles à long terme dans la maladie d'Erdheim-Chester ?
x.contexte:
La maladie d'Erdheim-Chester (MEC) est une histiocytose non langerhansienne rare, avec une incidence inférieure à 5 cas pour 10 millions d'adultes par an. Elle est caractérisée par l'accumulation d'histiocytes spumeux dans les os longs, les tissus rétropéritonéaux et périrénaux, le cœur, le système nerveux central et l'hypophyse. Les formes vont de l'atteinte localisée asymptomatique à l'atteinte multiviscérale sévère.

Elle est portée par des mutations activatrices des voies MAPK et PI3K-AKT, en particulier BRAF V600E, avec une inflammation systémique médiée par les cytokines. Le diagnostic repose sur les recommandations internationales (Goyal, Blood 2020).

Peu d'études ont évalué systématiquement le pronostic, et les facteurs connus, comme l'atteinte du système nerveux central, restent limités. Les conséquences sur la qualité de vie (handicap, dépression, troubles cognitifs) sont sous-estimées en pratique. Cette étude de cohorte coordonnée par le Meyer Children's Hospital IRCCS (Florence) vise à inclure 1 000 patients, prévalents et incidents, dans 7 centres de 4 pays, avec un suivi de 5 ans. Elle recueille les données cliniques, moléculaires, thérapeutiques et les questionnaires de qualité de vie.
x.interet: Un score pronostique fondé sur la survie et les résultats rapportés par les patients aiderait à stratifier les patients et à adapter la surveillance et le traitement. Il pourrait servir de base à de futurs essais dans une maladie très rare.
x.profil: Des patients (dès 7 ans) atteints de maladie d'Erdheim-Chester confirmée, prévalents et incidents.
inclusion: Consentement éclairé signé (parent ou représentant légal pour les mineurs)
Diagnostic de MEC confirmé selon les recommandations internationales les plus récentes
Données cliniques, moléculaires, thérapeutiques et de réponse disponibles
exclusion: Données diagnostiques ou de suivi manquantes
Refus ou impossibilité de signer le consentement

bras.traitement: Aucune intervention imposée ; consultations de suivi, recueil des données cliniques sur l'atteinte d'organes et la réponse au traitement, questionnaires de qualité de vie, origine géographique et survie

x.critere: Survie globale à 5 ans, et associations avec le groupe clinique, l'atteinte d'organes, le traitement, la réponse, la toxicité, les comorbidités et l'origine géographique
